pool.text: Khartoum was founded north of Soba by Muhammad Ali Pasha, incorporating Sudan into his realm.
Egypt shifted the seat of the colonial government from Wad Madani to Khartoum.
Heavy rains and floods destroyed most of the city of Khartoum.
European pressure forced Egypt to close the public slave market in Khartoum.
Samuel Baker visited Khartoum and observed that slavery was the main industry.
The Gordon Memorial College, now the University of Khartoum, was officially opened.
The population of Khartoum was estimated to have reached over fifty thousand people.
Khartoum was officially designated as the capital of an independent Republic of Sudan.
Rural to urban migration caused the population of Khartoum to balloon to one hundred eighty-five thousand.
Members of Black September held ten hostages at the Saudi Arabian embassy in Khartoum.
The first oil pipeline connecting Khartoum and Port Sudan was successfully completed.
Khartoum hosted the Organization of African Unity summit where Sudan was awarded the presidency.
Osama bin Laden purchased a residential house in the al-Riyadh neighborhood of Khartoum.
The death of John Garang triggered three days of violent riots across Khartoum.
The African Union and Arab League summits were held consecutively in Khartoum.
Major construction projects including the El Mek Nimr Bridge and Tuti Bridge were finished.
The Justice and Equality Movement engaged in armed combat against the Sudanese Armed Forces in Khartoum.
Sudan opened the Hotel Section and food court of the new Corinthia Hotel Tower.
An explosion at the Yarmouk munitions factory in Khartoum resulted in two deaths and one injury.
The Khartoum massacre occurred as security forces forcefully dispersed peaceful protests calling for civilian government.
